transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling a lot with talking excessively and constantly interrupting others. It's starting to cause some real issues in my daily interactions and relationships, so I wanted to get some help with it.
Have you struggled with this constant talking and interrupting since you were a child, or does it seem to happen in distinct periods or waves where you feel very different from your usual self?

This has definitely been a constant, ongoing struggle since I was a kid, rather than something that comes and goes in waves. Even back in elementary school, my teachers and parents always pointed out that I talked excessively and had a really hard time waiting my turn to speak. It has just always been this way for as long as I can remember.
Along with the talking and interrupting, do you also struggle with things like staying focused, organizing tasks, or frequently losing and forgetting things?

No, I don't really have much trouble with staying focused, organizing, or forgetting things. My main struggles are definitely just talking way too much and having a really hard time waiting my turn to speak.
Besides talking and interrupting, do you often find yourself fidgeting, feeling physically restless, or constantly on the go?

No, I don't really experience physical restlessness, fidgeting, or feeling like I'm constantly "on the go." For me, it's mostly verbal, like talking too much and really struggling to wait my turn to speak.
Do these struggles with talking and interrupting also cause difficulties for you at work or in school, or is it mainly limited to your personal relationships?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about it in that way, so I'm not sure if it affects one area more than the others. It just feels like a general struggle in my everyday life.

  "question": "Do you often find yourself getting up or leaving your seat in situations where you are expected to remain
No, I don't really struggle with staying in my seat. I can sit still just fine when I'm expected to, so that's not really an issue for me.
Do you find yourself blurting out answers before someone has even finished asking the question, or finishing other people's sentences for them?
I don't think I do that particularly often. I might talk a lot once I get started, but I don't usually find myself blurting out answers or finishing other people's sentences.
Do you find it difficult to engage in quiet leisure activities or hobbies, often feeling like you have to be doing something active or talkative instead?
I definitely talk excessively and find it really hard to remain quiet. However, I'm not sure if I have a general difficulty with quiet hobbies or if I feel a constant need to be physically active.
Do you often find it difficult to wait your turn in lines, games, or other group situations?

Yes, I find it extremely difficult to wait my turn, whether I'm standing in a line, playing a game, or waiting to speak in a group. It makes me feel incredibly impatient and restless inside when I have to wait. It has always been a major struggle for me.
Have colleagues at work or teachers in the past ever brought this up to you, or has it ever led to any formal issues or feedback in those settings?

Yes, absolutely. Ever since I was a kid in elementary school, my teachers constantly complained on my report cards that I talked too much during class and couldn't wait my turn. Even today at work, I still get similar feedback from colleagues and supervisors about my excessive talking and impatience.
